Need human decision for PR 11536. Basically I enable a new lint rule that checks for unused variables and clean up the repo. See more discussions there.

This lint rule is built-in, just disabled by default.

Better be quick before even more conflicts happen.
We also see a downside to enabling more lint rules: it requires widespread changes that can cause lots of merge conflicts.

Maybe I should do more marketing.

This lint rule detects let or have in whose names are completely unused.
In some cases this detects completely unused variable, such as:

diff --git a/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/F4/ShortRoot/Quotient/Pinning/DividedSquare.lean b/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/F4/ShortRoot/Quotient/Pinning/DividedSquare.lean
index 89f9c848..6cd17d39 100644
--- a/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/F4/ShortRoot/Quotient/Pinning/DividedSquare.lean
+++ b/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/F4/ShortRoot/Quotient/Pinning/DividedSquare.lean
@@ -165,10 +165,6 @@ theorem f4ShortRootQuotientToIdealEquiv_dividedSquare_rootColumn_of_long
       rw [hlift]
       exact f4ShortRootSubspace_mkQ_dividedSquare_rootVector_eq_zero_of_long
         k β hk hβ hβne
-    have htargetShort :
-        f4Length (f4SignedSimpleRootIndex (isogenyReverse k)) = 1 := by
-      rw [← f4SpecialIsogenyIndexEquiv_f4SignedSimpleRootIndex]
-      exact (f4Length_f4SpecialIsogenyIndexEquiv_eq_one_iff _).2 hk
     have htargetNe : i ≠
         f4OppositeRootIndex (f4SignedSimpleRootIndex (isogenyReverse k)) := by
       intro h

In other cases, the variables are implicitly used in some way, most commonly as an instance variable.
Then the variables are replaced with _:

       apply hia
       exact Subtype.ext h.symm
     · exact carPositiveRootPair_ne_reverse a i
-  · intro a ha x hx
+  · intro a _ x hx
     dsimp only [p, u, carOccupationEnd, carLoweringEnd] at hx ⊢
     simp only [Module.toModuleEnd_apply, DistribSMul.toLinearMap_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hx ⊢
     rw [← mul_assoc, carOccupationElement_mul_carGenerator_snd
       (ne_of_lt (mem_carPositiveRootPairs.mp a.2)), zero_mul]
-  · intro a ha x hx
+  · intro a _ x hx
     dsimp only [p, v, carOccupationEnd, carScaledRaisingEnd] at hx ⊢
     simp only [Module.toModuleEnd_apply, DistribSMul.toLinearMap_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hx ⊢
     rw [← mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm,
       carOccupationElement_mul_carGenerator_fst
         (ne_of_lt (mem_carPositiveRootPairs.mp a.2))]
-  · intro a ha x hx
+  · intro a _ x hx

(it's valid to ask whether _ha should be used instead of _ in the case above. Either way would have passed this lint rule.)
shouldnt these go to mathlib?
This particular lint rule is already in Lean (or mathlib? I forgot). It's just not enabled by default.
(I guess one reason is human wouldn't do unnecessary work)
Hmm ok, then maybe @Kim Morrison knows why its not enabled. I don't think this is a thing humans would just not do.

/-- Enables linting variables defined in tactic blocks, may be expensive for complex proofs -/
register_builtin_option linter.unusedVariables.analyzeTactics : Bool := {
  defValue := false
  descr := "enable analysis of local variables in presence of tactic proofs\
          \n\
          \nBy default, the linter will limit itself to linting a declaration's parameters \
            whenever tactic proofs are present as these can be expensive to analyze. Enabling this \
            option extends linting to local variables both inside and outside tactic proofs, \
            though it can also lead to some false negatives as intermediate tactic states may \
            reference some variables without the declaration ultimately depending on them."
}

It says two things: may be expensive for proof, and may have false negative. (False negative isn't an issue. Unless it means false positive?)

Maybe I should (have) git blame it.
git blame points to https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/5338 ...

Given that PR leads to mathlib being changed according to that rule, it's reasonable to say this lint rule is a good idea.
Performance-wise, it's probably cheaper than running the AI agents anyway.

On the other hand, if AI naturally write code that violate this lint rule, this will in turn lead to more token spend on AI agent...

But on a longer time horizon, code we write today will get into the training data for AI agents a few months later. If the AI companies survive that long, that is.

Any plan what to do with this? It's virtually impossible to keep the pull request free of merge conflicts, apparently. (Also it seems like leaving it open leads to at least some of the AI agents to notice the conflict and avoid working on similar parts...)
btw, you can use the linkifier, e.g. TauCeti#11536. (Making it easier for someone to click through makes it more likely they will merge. :-)
Yeah, I would definitely need to see some build time numbers before we could merge this. CI is about to become very expensive.
I suppose one alternative is simply to have “someone” do a run with the lint rule once in a while and send the fixes
“about to” become very expensive?
I'm certainly intending for https://taucetiproject.org/statistics/ to keep getting steeper (even after you take logs), via several mechanisms. One thing to announce, hopefully soon. :-)

To be fair, if incremental build is correctly implemented, per-PR build time should be like (c₁ ⋅ Δ code of that PR + c₂ ⋅ existing code), with c₁ ≫ c₂, and c₂ mostly on things like pulling the repo and such so independent of lint rules.

(Unless you change a fundamental definition, but if fundamental definitions are changed often then we have bigger problems…)

Agreed, but I do want to keep as a basic policy position that changes to fundamental definitions will always remain welcome. This has served Mathlib well over the years, and I'm confident it will serve us well too!

Maybe this one will need some more careful thought. For mathlib, the set of maintainers remain mostly the same, and so are their opinion on what is an improvement. What is to prevent one from (likely accidentally) DoS-ing the system by finding a cycle of changes to some basic definition that AI reviewer each agree that they're good, then indefinitely submit these?

(just for food of thought, but it certainly seems way more likely with AI reviewer than human reviewer)

Surprisingly, enabling this lint rule makes no measurable difference. (The one without the lint rule builds slower, but it's probably noise caused by something else running concurrently, and I don't really want to repeat the build, for each takes about 22 CPU hours…)

(there's some chance I make a mistake in the experiment, but I'm pretty sure not, I did comment out the weak.linter.unusedVariables.analyzeTactics = true and make a clean checkout both times, doubt that can go wrong)
The “10 merge conflicts per day” part is true, though I land https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/13836 for now, which should perhaps lessen the diff next time.
@Chris Birkbeck Why are you the only one to keep generating pull requests that mention https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/11536 (and all of them are refactor)?
I don't know, that's the red team working away
I'd just close the PR for now to avoid wasting tokens, I guess
